author: Alice Speri and Lex McMenamin
description:
Actor Susan Sarandon, whistleblower Chelsea Manning and comedian Caleb Hearon are detained by NYPD

More than 100 people were arrested outside the United Nations’ headquarters in New York City on Thursday as Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the general assembly, a speech that also prompted dozens of UN delegates to walk out in protest.

The protest outside the UN, one of several this week against the embattled Israeli prime minister, drew hundreds of Jewish, Palestinian, Iranian and Lebanese New Yorkers, among others, as well as several elected officials and candidates in the November election, and a number of celebrities.

Continue reading...
title: Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Holmes was sentenced to 11 years in prison in 2022 but has seen her sentenced reduced several times

Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of blood testing startup Theranos, will reportedly be transferred from a minimum security prison to a halfway home next August.

In 2022, Holmes, 42, was sentenced to more than 11 years in prison for defrauding Theranos investors out of hundreds of millions of dollars and ordered to pay restitution. The company falsely promoted its technology as being capable of detecting diseases, including types of cancer, from drops of finger-pricked blood.

Continue reading...
title: Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes reportedly to be transferred to halfway home next year

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Industry leaders call on government to protect homegrown produce in the interest of national security

The gap between Britain’s food and drink exports and imports has neared its highest this century, as a combination of Brexit, war in the Middle East and US tariffs dented deliveries overseas while imports soared.

The UK’s food and drink trade deficit has risen to more than £21bn – the largest since 2000 – in what industry leaders said was a “wake-up call” for the government to protect homegrown produce in the interest of national security.

Continue reading...
title: UK food and drink trade deficit largest since 2000 at £21bn

author: Associated Press
description:
James Copenhaver, 76, was left with lingering injuries after gunman opened fire from rooftop at Butler rally

James Copenhaver, one of three campaign rally attendees shot in 2024 during an assassination attempt on then candidate Donald Trump, has died in Pittsburgh, his lawyer said Thursday. He was 76.

Copenhaver was in the bleachers during the event in Butler, Pennsylvania, when a 20-year-old gunman opened fire from a nearby rooftop, grazing Trump’s right ear with one bullet. Copenhaver was struck in the arm and in the abdomen, wounds that left him with lingering injuries and walking with a cane.

Continue reading...
title: Man shot and wounded during Trump assassination attempt dies in Pennsylvania

author: Guardian moderators (now); Joseph Gedeon, Dara Kerr and Chris Stein (from 11am EDT)
description:
Who are the groups backing candidates in the midterms – and why? In our second live discussion ahead of the elections, Joseph Gedeon, Dara Kerr and Chris Stein will join us at 11am EDT on Friday 25 September to answer your questions about who is supporting the November races

Welcome to our second live Q&A about the upcoming midterm elections. Today, our reporters will be joining us to answer your questions about who is funding the campaigns, where the money is going and how it’s shaping the election outlook ahead of the votes on 3 November.

In the past few months our reporting team has covered in depth:

How major companies that urged Congress to strengthen the Voting Rights Act continue to contribute to state political groups that are actively working to undermine the legislation.

The vast extent of spending by
title: Reader Q&A: who’s spending big on the midterms? Our reporters take your questions

author: Sam Levine
description:
State election officials said they reviewed 185 records homeland security sent them and confirmed they were US citizens

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) wrongly identified 185 people on Nevada’s voter rolls as non-citizens, state officials said this week, escalating concerns over the shoddy methodology the government is using to raise fear about non-citizen voting ahead of the midterm elections.

In July, Donald Trump gave a speech saying DHS had found a combined 278,000 non-citizens on the rolls in Nevada, California, Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Follow-up letters to each of those states weakened the claim, saying there only could be as many as 278,000 non-citizens on the rolls, including up to 15,903 in Nevada.

Continue reading...
title: Nearly 200 people wrongly identified on Nevada’s voter rolls as non-citizens

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Alaska Democratic nominee in pivotal Senate race ‘struggled to deal with her grief’ after death of husband and mother, spokesperson said

Mary Peltola’s campaign on Thursday downplayed a report that the Democratic nominee in Alaska’s pivotal Senate race shoved a staffer and used slurs, saying the article exaggerated her behavior, but acknowledging she struggled following the deaths of her husband and mother.

The New York Times article published on Wednesday is based on text messages and interviews with nine former employees of Peltola, who served in the House of Representatives from 2022 till the beginning of last year and is now set to face the Republican senator Dan Sullivan in the 3 November midterm elections.

Continue reading...
title: Mary Peltola’s campaign says reports of her using slurs and shoving staffer are exaggerated

author: Nick Visser
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Falling meth prices help drive deaths to record levels

Falling methamphetamine prices have helped push overdose deaths to record levels, new data shows.

In fact, several of the indicators are now at the highest observed levels that we’ve seen, including wastewater, consumption, methamphetamine-related hospitalisations, and death.

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: Paterson says PM’s AI hack timing not a coincidence; gen Z going without for a house

author: Anna Bawden and Denis Campbell
description:
Patient groups decry ‘scandalous’ delays as four integrated care boards take step due to soaring demand for diagnoses

NHS bodies are forcing people with suspected attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism to wait at least two years before they can be assessed as they struggle to meet surging demand for diagnoses of neurodiversity.

Four NHS integrated care boards (ICBs) covering large regions of England have adopted the approach because they cannot afford the cost of the number of assessments that people are seeking.

Continue reading...
title: NHS bodies in England impose two-year minimum wait for ADHD and autism assessments

author: Sam Levine
description:
Crystal Mason has spent nearly a decade fighting conviction for casting provisional ballot that ultimately wasn’t counted

The nearly decade-long case of a Black Texas woman who was sentenced to five years in prison in a controversial illegal voting case will end with an acquittal, the state’s highest criminal court said in a 5-4 decision on Thursday.

The woman, Crystal Mason, has been appealing against the case ever since her 2018 conviction for casting a provisional ballot that ultimately wasn’t counted. In 2024, the Texas court of criminal appeals acquitted her in the case. The local prosecutor handling the case appealed that ruling to Texas’s highest criminal court, w
title: Texas woman triumphs as court upholds acquittal in voting error case

author: Patrick Wintour in New York
description:
Senior Iranian officials say Washington has four to five days to respond to its conditions for reopening the strait

The UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has met his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, for the first time in New York amid warnings from senior Iranian security officials that the US has four to five days to respond to its conditions for reopening the strait of Hormuz.

The previously unknown apparent deadline was specified by Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of the supreme national security council, in a TV interview on Wednesday evening, and it is unclear what action Tehran will take if the US does not respond to Iran’s preconditions for reopening the vital waterway.

Continue reading...
title: Ed Miliband meets Iran’s foreign minister as Tehran gives US ultimatum on strait of Hormuz

author: Joseph Gedeon and Chris Stein in Washington
description:
GOP stymies House-passed war powers resolution as conflict passes 200-day mark with 19 US service members killed

Senate Republicans on Thursday blocked a Democratic effort to end the US war with Iran, voting 49-50 against a House-passed war powers resolution as the conflict passed the 200-day mark, with 19 American service members killed.

The measure passed the House earlier with bipartisan support. Senate Democrats, led by the minority leader, Chuck Schumer, and the senator Andy Kim of New Jersey, forced the vote under the War Powers Resolution, which allows lawmakers to bring such measures to the floor.

Continue reading...
title: Senate Republicans block Democratic effort to end US war with Iran

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
State supreme court rules Chad Bianco’s conduct unlawful and says he ‘must refrain from further handling’ of ballots

A Republican California sheriff must return more than a half-million ballots he seized for an investigation into unfounded voting improprieties in a special election last year, the state supreme court ruled Thursday.

Riverside county sheriff Chad Bianco in February seized approximately 650,000 ballots from a November 2025 special election on statewide congressional redistricting favorable to Democrats and pushed by Governor Gavin Newsom. The measure easily passed statewide, and won in Bianco’s county by roughly 80,000 votes.

Continue reading...
title: California sheriff ordered to return ballots he confiscated in voter ‘fraud’ inquiry

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
US GAO documents array of costly problems as ICE pursues controversial plans to rapidly increase detention capacity

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and other federal agencies have wasted tens of millions of dollars pursuing controversial plans to rapidly increase detention capacity – and the total will likely rise due to ongoing mismanagement, congressional investigators warned on Thursday.

The US Government Accountability Office (GAO) documented costly problems in several initiatives ICE has pursued since Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025 and ordered the mass arrest and deportation of people whom his administration has deemed should be
title: ICE has wasted tens of millions to carry out Trump’s mass detention agenda – report

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
Deference was deafening as US president rolled out red carpet for world’s biggest jailer of journalists – perhaps he was seeking tips

One is an authoritarian who represses the media with a strong allergy to democratic elections. The other is head of the Chinese Communist party.

Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, to the White House on Thursday, setting the stage for a scene quite unlike anything the august old building has seen over more than two centuries.

Continue reading...
title: Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
‘If you’re not in the internal market, you don’t get the same protection,’ says French minister of policy designed to curb Chinese competition

France is leading a push to exclude the UK from the EU’s “Made in Europe” policy that could result in British companies losing out in the race to supply European countries with low-carbon technologies and electric cars.

The plans were raised by Andy Burnham when he met the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, on the sidelines of the UN general assembly earlier this week.

Continue reading...
title: France says EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ law should not include the UK

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Datacentre hailed by government was supposed to start operating next year but may be held back into mid-2030s

A huge datacentre project hailed by the UK government will miss its launch date next year and could be delayed into the mid-2030s.

The site in Loughton, Essex, was described as the country’s largest AI supercomputer when it was announced in 2025, but power supply problems mean it now faces a lengthy wait before coming online.

Continue reading...
title: Launch of UK’s ‘largest AI supercomputer’ delayed by power supply problems

author: Nick Visser
description:
Three million chickens a week will be processed at the state-of-the-art facility in Tamworth – a fifth of all those eaten nationwide

It is for birds? Is it for planes?

The sleek, rust-coloured saucer settles into the earth, mirroring the surrounding hills. It looks like an art gallery or a high-end conference centre – an architectural masterpiece designed to sit lightly on the land.

Continue reading...
title: Australia’s newest chicken factory looks like a modern art gallery – but will it improve animal welfare?

description:
Council on AI Strategy chief says incident unlikely to be isolated and country should enhance capability to detect and report incidents

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Technology experts have warned revelations an artificial intelligence agent hacked Medicare’s internal systems will not be the only dangerous breach of government data and have called for Australia to boost its protections against the growing risk.

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, challenged the OpenAI boss, Sam Altman, on Thursday after the company’s agent infiltrated systems run by the Australian Inst
title: AI hack of Medicare exposes Australia’s vulnerabilities and experts warn ‘there is more of this to come’

author: Benita Kolovos and Bertin Huynh
description:
Ombudsman finds government breached teen’s human rights, saying the conditions ‘bordered on solitary confinement’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A 16-year-old boy was held in conditions akin to solitary confinement in adult prison for 22 hours a day, leading him to have suicidal thoughts, a Victorian ombudsman report has revealed.

The report, tabled in parliament on Thursday, found the Department of Justice and Community Safety breached the teen’s human rights when transferring him from the Parkville Youth Justice Precinct to the maximum-security
title: Boy, 16, held in ‘cramped’ prison cell alone for 22 hours a day for weeks, Victorian ombudsman finds

author: Jillian Ambrose
description:
US president’s suggested 90-day export ban before midterm elections could bring even higher fuel prices across Europe

  • Business live – latest updates

The EU has warned Donald Trump against plans to ban US diesel exports to the global market, saying the move would negatively affect Europe and the US.

The European Commission has reacted with “concern” to reports this week that the US president could prevent diesel from reaching the global market.

Continue reading...
title: EU says Trump plan to ban US diesel exports would ‘negatively impact both sides’

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Clip of the former Tory MP staring intently at fellow panellist is shared widely online

Rory Stewart has been an Afghan NGO leader, a Conservative leadership candidate, a Harvard professor, a popular podcaster, and the deputy governor of an Iraqi province. This week, he created a moment that drew wider attention than any of them: he fixed a beady gaze on a fellow Newsnight panellist for the longest four seconds in television history.

Stewart, who now co-presents The Rest Is Politics with Alastair Campbell, appeared on the BBC programme on 18 September – but in the last few days, a clip of the moment in question has taken on a life of its own on social media.

Continue reading...
title: The eyes have it: Rory Stewart’s ‘magnificently strange’ Newsnight moment goes viral

author: Maya Yang
description:
Senators’ report says taxpayers face higher bills after ‘bargain’ between president and major polluters

The fossil fuel industry secured an estimated $190bn in tax breaks and subsidies over the next decade after responding to Donald Trump’s pre-election call for major campaign donations, leaving American taxpayers to shoulder higher bills and public health costs associated with pollution, according to a new report.

Released on Thursday by Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, ranking member of the Senate environment and public works committee, and Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, the report details what the senators describe as the fossil fuel industry’s expansive influence over the Trump administration.

Continue reading...
title: Fossil-fuel firms in line for billions in benefits after answering Trump’s donation call

author: Martin Belam
description:
State visit takes place at same time as UN general assembly, which Chinese leader has avoided. Plus, meet the people who are real-life Pokémon ‘professors’

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Donald Trump has welcomed Xi Jinping to the US, greeting the Chinese leader on the asphalt at Joint Base Andrews at the start of his state visit. Xi’s trip coincides with the UN general assembly in New York, but he is not attending the gathering.

The pageantry will continue with a formal welcome on the South Lawn of the White House, private tea with the US president and first lady, and a tour of the National Archives, among other special events. The White House also invited major tech leaders to a state dinner bei
title: First Thing: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington amid tensions over trade, AI and Taiwan

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Unions say record high figures, including assaults on rail workers as well as members of public, show need for more staff and policing

  • Business live – latest updates

The number of reported assaults on Britain’s railways has risen to a record high of almost 25,000 incidents in a year.

Unions said the “horrendous” figures showed the need for more staff and policing, as the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) revealed a sharp increase in assaults on the travelling public and on railway staff last year.

Continue reading...
title: Reported assaults on Britain’s railways rise to nearly 25,000 a year

author: Chris Hippensteel
description:
Federal judge ordered Trump administration to immediately return the outlets’ press passes and issued a temporary restraining order that will be in effect for 14 days

  • Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Yesterday evening, after briefly taking the case under consideration, a federal judge ordered the White House to temporarily restore access to CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, the three outlets the president banned from the building via a social media post last week.

White House security may not have gotten the memo, according to a new story from Politi
title: Trump’s ban on CNN, Politico and MS Now likely unconstitutional, judge rules in restoring temporary access – US politics live

author: Martin Farrer
description:
The 11-year-old died at Westmead children’s hospital three days after incident at a unit in Norwest

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A young boy who was allegedly shot at a home in Sydney’s north-west earlier this week has died.

Police said that the boy, who had been in a critical condition since being found with a gunshot wound at a unit in Norwest on Monday, died in hospital at about 8pm on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Boy, 11, shot in the face and neck in Sydney dies from his injuries

description:
Rising cost of 10-year gilt to near 19-year high hikes upfront cost of government investment and limits chancellor’s room for manoeuvre

  • Business live – latest updates

  • International bodies warn of rising debt and borrowing risks

  • Burnham stands by claim UK is ‘in hock’ to bond markets

A global sell-off in government bonds has put fresh upward pressure on UK borrowing costs, before a tough budget for John Healey next month.

The yield – effectively the interest rate – on 10-year UK bonds, known as gilts, had risen to 5.38% by mid-morning on Thursday, a
title: Global bond sell-off piles new pressure on UK borrowing costs before budget

author: Catie McLeod
description:
One-year-old dies after alleged attack on Sunday, while three-year-old sibling remains in critical condition

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A baby has died in a Sydney hospital five days after a mother allegedly stabbed them and two other children in the Blue Mountains, police say.

Bystanders were first on the scene after finding the three children and the 42-year-old woman with stab wounds inside a vehicle at Valley Heights in the Blue Mountains, west of Sydney, on Sunday afternoon.

Continue reading...
title: Second child dies after alleged Blue Mountain stabbing as mother faces additional murder charge

author: Rachel Hall
description:
Former deputy PM now involved in tech industry says many within the sector are ‘winding themselves up into a lather’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Nick Clegg has dismissed fears over AI’s “godlike power to exterminate humanity”, calling it a sign that tech bosses are “breathing their own fumes”.

The former UK deputy prime minister said that tech bosses should focus on addressing known “specific threats” such as cybersecurity, bio-weapons and emotional dependence rather than the “slightly hand-wavy view that this technology is unavoidably going to develop some godlike power which is going to turn on us and exterminate humanity”.

Continue reading...<
title: Nick Clegg plays down fears ‘godlike’ AI could exterminate humanity

author: Jessica Elgot and Ashley Kirk
description:
Polling suggests Andy Burnham is attracting progressives back to Labour, motivated by desire to stop Nigel Farage

• How Labour’s majority depends on five progressive voter types – in charts

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Progressive voters could push Reform UK into fourth place and put Labour within touching distance of a majority if tactical voting is widespread at the next election, a major poll has found.

Andy Burnham is beginning to attract a significant number of left-leaning voters back to Labour, motivated by a desire to stop Nigel Farage, the results suggest.
title: Tactical voting at next election could push Reform into fourth place, poll finds

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Firm unveils further cost-cutting plan including job losses blaming poor summer sales of private homes

  • Business live – latest updates

Vistry Group, one of Britain’s biggest housebuilders, has slashed its annual profit expectations after half-year losses ballooned as it grappled with a £600m pile of unsold homes.

Adam Daniel, the new chief executive of the Bovis Homes and Countryside owner, insisted that “the issues can be fixed”, as he set out a detailed turnaround plan that involves pulling out of private sales in south-east England and slimming operations to turn Vistry into a more focused, 12,000-homes-a-year builder.
title: Housebuilder Vistry slashes profit forecasts as losses balloon

author: Achol Arok
description:
Four occupants of bus taken to hospital after multi-vehicle crash in Glenburn

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A woman has died and several others injured after a multi-vehicle collision in Victoria’s Yarra Ranges involving a bus carrying 18 people.

Emergency services responded to reports of a three-vehicle crash, including a commercial bus, on the Melba Highway at Glenburn at about 2.40pm.

Continue
title: Woman dead and multiple people injured after bus collides with two cars in Victoria

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Victoria’s anti-corruption body charges the ex-staffer with seven counts of theft and one count of misconduct in public office

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former senior National Gallery of Victoria employee is alleged to have funnelled $8m from the gallery over six years.

He allegedly bought $8m worth of mobile phones using an NGV account, which he then sold for personal gain.
title: National Gallery of Victoria employee allegedly stole $8m to buy phones he later sold

author: Emma Joyce explains it to Steph Harmon
description:
For the first time in recent history there’ll be no pre-game entertainment at the NRL grand final. But everyone has a different story about what actually went down

Emma, the NRL and Tones and I seem to be at war – but I can’t make sense of what’s going on.

I’ll try to catch you up. The Dance Monkey singer made headlines this week after it was leaked she’d turned down an offer to perform at next weekend’s NRL grand final. The rugby league boss Peter V’landys said negotiations broke down due to “artistic differences”, and some claimed it was because the Aria award-winning artist didn’t want to play her biggest hit.

Continue reading...
title: Dance Monkey v the NRL: did Tones and I really turn down $90,000 a minute because she hates her own song?

description:
Fuel costs have risen to levels not seen since early April, adding to risk of inflation and interest rate hike

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian diesel prices could surge above $3 a litre if Donald Trump cuts off US diesel exports amid floundering negotiations with Iran.

Fuel costs have risen to levels not seen since early April, adding to inflation risks and making another hike in interest rates all but certain.
title: Diesel prices across Australia could surge beyond $3 a litre as Trump eyes cut to US fuel exports

But Kyriakos Mitsotakis says he cannot accept any arrangement that recognises British Museum’s ownership of the sculptures

  • Kyriakos Mitsotakis: Britain would not cut up the Bayeux tapestry. So seize this moment and reunite the Parthenon sculptures in Greece

The Greek prime minister has said a deal can still be reached to return the Parthenon marbles with “political will” but his country will not accept a loan in the style of the Bayeux tapestry’s visit from France.

Writing for the Guardian, Kyriakos Mitsotakis said Greece “cannot accept any arrangement that would require it to recognise the British Museum’s ownership of the sculptures, or a
title: Greek PM: deal to return Parthenon marbles could still be reached with ‘political will and courage’

author: Sandra Laville
description:
Exclusive: Levy that allows almost 16,000 houses to be built on Norfolk Broads will not cover cost of mitigating environmental damage, critics say

A new levy on developers to allow almost 16,000 homes to be built in the environmentally protected Norfolk Broads has been cut by tens of thousands of pounds per house, the Guardian can reveal.

Ministers say the government’s environmental delivery plans (EDPs) were created to unblock housing growth across the country and are a “win-win” for development and nature.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Cash to trash’ levy on house developers too low to offset damage to Norfolk Broads, say critics

author: Phillip Inman
description:
IPPR finds failure to align testing standards has forced companies to abandon exporting to EU and is costing costing 0.18% of national income

The UK is losing out on annual exports to the EU that could be worth as much as £6.5bn without a deal with Brussels that allows manufacturers to jettison duplicate product testing.

In the latest attempt to calculate the loss of trade with the EU after Brexit, the IPPR thinktank said many companies have given up selling goods to the EU or set up subsidiaries inside the trade bloc after successive governments failed to secure a mutual recognition agreement that would avoid the extra administration costs.

Motor vehicle and part exports would have been between £2.48bn and £3.42bn higher each year.

Electronic exports could have been between £1.17bn and £1.67bn higher.

Pharmaceutical exports would have had an estimated annual uplift of between £740m and £820m.
title: UK losing up to £6.5bn a year in EU trade due to mismatched product rules

description:
Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching, including two charges involving the athlete

The man who was Alan Jones’s butler for almost two decades has told a Sydney court his boss would welcome a prominent athlete to his luxury harbourside apartment with “a hug and a slap on the bottom” and would call him “cham
title: Alan Jones welcomed prominent athlete to luxury home with ‘hug and slap on the bottom’, former butler tells court

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies before concealing bodies in bags purchased from sports store

Beau Lamarre-Condon was seen sizing up a surfboard bag used to dispose of a victim days before the police officer murdered two men, prosectors have alleged in a Sydney court, with chilling CCTV footage shown to the jury.

Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, with his police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon sized up surfboard bag against friend before allegedly murdering Sydney couple, court told

author: Jonathan Barrett
description:
Dockers supporters cannot buy a barrel of Woodside oil – but the fossil fuel company hopes to buy into fans’ loyalty

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When an oil and gas company buys logo space on an AFL jersey, it isn’t trying to convince fans to buy its products.

Fremantle Dockers supporters cannot, for example, go to their local service station to buy a barrel of Woodside Energy oil or a canister of its liquefied natural gas.
title: Why is Woodside sponsoring Fremantle’s AFL team – and will the climate crisis shift the relationship?
